newsitem.title: USA: Mass. governor pushes $1.4 mln cable tv tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Mass. governor pushes $1.4 mln cable tv tax cut.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. Paul Cellucci on Monday filed legislation that would eliminate the state's $1.4 million tax on cable television operations and restructure the industry to allow for increased competition.

Massachusetts families spend $728 million annually on cable television or an average of $33 a month, Cellucci told reporters, after expressing his own frustration "at having to wait two years to get ESPN2" to watch University of Massachusetts basketball games.
His local cable company did not offer the sports station.

Cellucci says the new bill, in addition to eliminating the $0.80 per customer tax levied on cable operators and passed on to consumers, would reform the cable industry by reducing the time and expense necessary to receive a cable license, establish statewide licenses and encourage new companies, such as telephone companies and utilities, to enter the market.
